title: Siliguri
text:
Siliguri (Bengali: শিলিগুড়ি Shiliguṛi, Hindi: सिलीगुड़ी Silīguṛī), the largest city in northern West Bengal, is a liberal and cosmopolitan city that is known for its vibrant music scene and strong youth culture. On the banks of the Mahananda River and the Teesta River at the foothills of the Darjeeling Hills, Siliguri is the third-largest urban agglomeration in West Bengal. It is known as the "Gateway of North-Eastern India" as it connects North-Eastern India with the mainland through a narrow strip of land, making it a major trading and transport hub. It borders Nepal on one side and Bangladesh on the other.


== Understand ==

Siliguri (Bengali: শিলিগুড়ি SHEE-lee-GOO-ree) has a population of nearly a million (2025), making it the third-largest city in West Bengal.
With massive developments since the turn of the 21st century, the city has grown from a small regional town into one of the most important business centres in Eastern India. Sprawling and boisterous, it is a city whose periphery is dominated by modern condominiums, while the centre is characterised by sprawling street markets, up-scale shops, and large shopping malls.
Due to its position as a commercial hub and centre of learning, the city enjoys a sophistication and range of shopping usually only associated with metro cities. Furthermore, as it has attracted a large number of young Nepalese, Sikkimese, Tibetans, and Bhutanese, it has developed into one of India's most liberal and cosmopolitan cities that is known for its vibrant music scene and strong youth culture.


=== Name and history ===

The name "Siliguri" means a "stack of pebbles" in Bengali.
Siliguri was a small agricultural village at the foothills of the Himalayas, predominantly inhabited by the Kirati and Lepcha peoples in the late 18th century. At the time, Phansidewa, located south of Siliguri, was a major river port on the Mahananda River, serving as a trading hub with Bihar, Malda, and South Bengal. The hill tribes of Darjeeling regularly used the port to ship agricultural produce.
Following the Anglo-Nepalese Treaty of Sugauli in 1816, Siliguri rapidly developed as a transit point to the hills and Nepal. In 1865, the British acquired Darjeeling and the Dooars to develop tea gardens for export to England. To facilitate the growing tea trade, the narrow-gauge Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (DHR) was constructed between Siliguri and Darjeeling in 1880.
Following the partition of Bengal in 1947, a narrow strip of land known as the Siliguri Corridor, or Chicken's Neck, became strategically important. The corridor connects North-Eastern India with the rest of the country. In the years that followed, many refugees from East Bengal and migrants from Northeast India settled in and around Siliguri, attracted by its comparatively well-developed infrastructure. As the existing rail links to the Northeast were severed by the partition, a new metre-gauge railway connecting Siliguri and Assam was established in 1951. A decade later, the broad-gauge New Jalpaiguri Junction (NJP) was built, becoming Siliguri's principal railway station and strengthening rail connectivity between Northeast India and the rest of the country. The metre-gauge line was subsequently converted to broad gauge, leaving the colonial-era DHR as the only non-broad-gauge railway in North Bengal.


=== Economy ===
Siliguri is the only city in West Bengal other than Kolkata to have an international airport and, perhaps due to the high concentration of colleges and private schools, the city has the highest literacy rates in the state.
Siliguri's traditional economy is based around the three 'T's: tea, timber and tourism. After the parition in 1947, Siliguri eaned the fourth 'T', that is "transport", as it has become the sole gateway to Darjeeling, Sikkim, Bhutan and North-Eastern India.


=== Climate ===

Siliguri has a warm summer, cool winters and a severe monsoon. In summer, the temperature varies from a minimum of 18-22 °C to a maximum of 26-32 °C. The temperature in summer sometimes exceeds 35 °C. On the other hand, the winter maximum temperature hovers around 20-24 °C, and the minimum drops 6-9 °C. January is the coldest month with an average temperature of 16.1 °C. The minimum temperature in winter season sometimes drops 5 °C or below. On an average, Siliguri gets 3340 mm per year. Winters are mostly dry, with the summers being rainy. About 80% of the annual rainfall is felt between June to September, this period is known as monsoons or rainy season in the season cycle. Heavy showers are often felt in May, June, July, August and September. July is the wettest month (804 mm) and January is the driest month (12 mm).


=== Visitor information ===
1 Tourism Centre, M-4 Bldg, Hill Cart Road, ☏ +91 353 2511974, +91 353 2516306. The staff at the Tourism Centre is very helpful and the centre has a lot of information on North Bengal tourism. You can book a government lodge there before travelling to your favourite destination. (updated Nov 2022)


== Talk ==
Bengali is the main language of Siliguri. Hindi, English, and Nepali are also understood by many people. As a major trading hub the city has drawn people from a wide range of ethnic backgrounds. So it's not uncommon to hear other languages in the streets, like Bhojpuri and Rajasthani.


== Get in ==


=== By plane ===
1 Bagdogra International Airport (IXB  IATA), Bagdogra (14 km (8.7 mi) from the city centre), ☏ +91 353 269 8431. The airport has links with most major Indian cities: Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata and Guwahati. In addition, a number of airlines operate connecting flights from Bangkok, while Druk Air offers twice in a week direct flights to the Thai capital, which begin and terminate in Paro with a stop here. Taxis are available from the airport to Siliguri (approx ₹500), as well as to Darjeeling, Gangtok, and Phuentsholing. (updated Nov 2022)


=== By train ===
Siliguri is served by four Rajdhani Express trains, two Vistadome Express trains, two Humsafar Express trains, four AC Superfast Express trains, a Shatabdi Express train, and a Vande Bharat Express train. There's also the Mitali Express from Bangladesh.


==== New Jalpaiguri Junction ====
2 New Jalpaiguri Junction  NFR  DHR  (code: NJP) (about 20- to 30-minute ride from the city centre). The busiest railway station in North Bengal with connections to almost all parts of India. NJP has two double-bedded air-conditioned (AC) retiring rooms, six double-bedded non-AC retiring rooms, one three-bedded dormitory and one twelve-bedded dormitory. Free high-speed Wi-Fi is available at this station. It has IRCTC and other private restaurants. There is also a decommissioned train coach that acts as a restaurant, and tea rooms that serve locally grown tea. The tourist office and pre-paid taxi booth are directly opposite the station main entrance. (updated Sep 2025)
Transport options to city centre:

By bus: North Bengal State Transport Corporation (NBSTC) operates bus services from NJP to Siliguri city centre. There are private bus options as well.
By taxi: Ride-hailing services, such as Uber, Rapido and Ola, provide rides from NJP to various parts of the city. Apart from these, numerous private taxi operators provide pre-paid and post-paid taxi services to the city.


==== Other stations ====
3 Siliguri Junction  NFR  DHR  (code: SGUJ). Although mostly servicing local routes, Siliguri Junction also has a few long-distance trains, including the Mahananda Express (from New Delhi) and the Kanchankanya Express (from Sealdah). Another interchange between broad-gauge and narrow-gauge lines. The station has a pleasant tea room serving locally grown tea just outside the main entrance. (updated Oct 2022)
4 Siliguri Town  NFR  DHR  (code: SGUT). The original gateway to the Darjeeling Hills. (updated Dec 2022)


=== By bus ===
From Dhaka: Under a joint understanding between Indian and Bangladeshi transport authority, there are regular bus services from Dhaka, capital of Bangladesh. BRTC (Bangladesh Road Transport Corporation) buses leave Dhaka every night at 8PM and reach India-Bangladesh border at Changrabanda post at early morning. These buses will not cross the border and the passengers have to clear customs, walk a few hundred yards to cross the border and board the waiting Indian buses for another three-hour ride to Siliguri. The buses are air conditioned, very comfortable and depart on time. One-way fare from Dhaka to Siliguri is between US$20-25, depending on conversion rates.
From Kathmandu: Greenline operates a daily overnight A/C Volvo bus service from Kathmandu (Swayambhu Bus Stand) to Siliguri (Tenzing Norgay Bus Station). Departs at 3PM, arriving at 8:30AM. ₹2,000. The Nepal-Indian border at Siliguri, which was only open to Bhutanese, Indian, and Nepalese passport holders since the pandemic, is now open to all passport holders with valid visas. (updated May 2025)
From Kolkata: The well-known and comfortable Siliguri Rocket, run by the North Bengal State Transport Corporation (NBSTC), leaves Kolkata at 8PM arriving Siliguri at 8AM (₹245). Some of the private bus lines also ply the route. The 'Royal Cruiser' Volvo buses leaves Kolkata at 8PM arriving Siliguri at 9AM (₹745 AC/₹325 non-AC).
From Phuentsholing: Khorlo/Dophu Transport (+975 77870211). Daily: 7:30AM (Eicher bus), 8AM (Coaster bus) 3PM (Coaster bus) - Nu350 - a four-hour journey. Unlike other out-of-town bus services, the one from Phuentsholing does not terminate at Tenzing Norgay Bus Terminus, but at a bus stand opposite Golden Plaza on Burdwan Road (behind Air View More) (updated June 2026)


==== Stations ====
5 Tenzing Norgay Bus Terminus, Hill Cart Road, Pradhan Nagar. The terminus operates a dormitory for passengers on 2F (booking in terminus) - 12 hours for ₹300 - and a waiting lounge with sofas and mobile phone charging facilities. (updated Sep 2026)
6 P. C. Mittal Memorial Bus Terminus.  (updated Jul 2026)
7 Sikkim Nationalised Transport Bus Terminus (SNT Bus Terminus) (near the Tenzing Norgay Bus Terminus).  (updated Jul 2026)


== Get around ==

Moving in and around Siliguri is cheap. There are electric rickshaws (locally known as totos), shared vans, an efficient public bus service, and rental cars. 
App-based car services are also available on Yatri Saathi, Rapido (also bikes) and Uber. 
Shared e-rickshaws and vans run on established routes: Standard fare: ₹20 per person (₹10 for short routes,  ₹30 for long ones) - as of 2025. 
The core areas can be covered on foot and is very safe, even after dark. 


== See ==


=== Monasteries and temples ===
1 Buddha Mundir Monastery, Buddha Mundir Road, Salbari (Salibari). A monastery established by the Nyingma yogi, Chatral Sangye Dorji Rinpoche 
2 Ewam (Nupchen Namchak) Monastery (Toribari Gompa), Junglee Mohal, Toribari Village, Bhaktinagar (behind Bengal Safari P.O P.S), ☏ +91 353 259 0264. A large Buddhist monastery in the Nyingma tradition. (updated Jul 2026)
3 ISKCON Temple, Iskcon Road, Ward 41, Haidar Par, ☏ +91 92316 84759. It houses many beautiful idols of Advaita Acharya, Lord Narasimha, Lord Chaitanya and many more. 
4 Khordong Byangter Monastery, Dhansara (on road to Darjeeling, near NJP Station), ☏ +91 99330 62222, +91 98320 49416. A monastery is in the Nyingma tradition of Tibetan Buddhism. Accommodation available at the compound. 
5 Tashi Gomang Shedra Buddhist Monastery (Salugara Monastery), Salugara (15 - 20 minutes from city centre). Inaugurated by the Dalai Lama in 1999, and belongs to the Kagyu tradition of Tibetan Buddhism. (updated Jul 2026)
6 Triratna Monastery, Salbari (15 - 20 minutes' drive from city centre). A monastery in the Nyingma tradition of Tibetan Buddhism (updated Mar 2018)


=== Museums ===
7 North Bengal Science Centre, Matigara. The campus has a museum, a planetarium and an Interpretation Centre that displays various type of flora. (updated Jul 2026)


== Do ==
There are many places in Siliguri to visit and spend some quality time. You can tour the city yourself by renting a bike or a car. There are many places to watch movies. You can also visit tea estates for a tour where you can see the serene and spacious tea farms in and around the city. There are many exhibitions and sport events around the city.


=== Parks ===
1 Dreamland Amusement Park, Ghoshpukur Canal Road, Fulbari, ☏ +91 97328 51000, dreamland.slg@gmail.com. 10AM-7PM. An amusement and theme park. 
2 North Bengal Wild Animals' Park (Bengal Safari Park), 5 Mile, Salugara, ☏ +91-7047312620, info@northbengalwildanimalspark.in. The Siliguri section of the Mahananda Wildlife Sanctuary with tigers, leopards, elephants, and herbivorous. Elephant rides. Forest park setting. ₹200 (half hour), ₹400 (one hour). (updated Jul 2026)
3 Savin Kingdom, Darjeeling More, ☏ +91 353 251 4228, gmsavinkingdom@gmail.com. Daily 10:30AM-6PM. Dagapur (near Darjeeling More). An amusement and water park among tea plantations. (updated Oct 2016)
4 Surya Sen Park, Janta Nagar. Daily 3-7PM. A river runs along this park with kids’ rides, play equipment, shade trees and a miniature train. It also hosts many alternative energy exhibitions and picnic areas. (updated Jul 2026)


=== Events ===
The North Bengal Book Fair takes place at the Kanchanjunga Stadium Fair Ground for the first two weeks of December. It is a significant cultural event in the city.


== Buy ==

Siliguri's commercial activities are primarily concentrated along three main streets: Hill Cart Road, Bidhan Road, and Sevoke Road. Hill Cart Road is lined with traditional shops and is home to many of the city's hotels, as well as its main inter-state bus terminal. Sevoke Road features several upscale shopping malls and serves as the city's banking hub, while Bidhan Road is best known for the bustling street markets that meander through the surrounding lanes.
As the centre of a tea-growing area, Siliguri is an excellent place to pick up some Darjeeling and other brands of the leaf.


=== Books ===
Crossword Book Stores, City Centre and Vega Circle Mall. Commercial bookstores with a focus on fiction. Selection of stationary.


=== Handicrafts ===
1 Fab India, Times Square Building, Sevoke Road and City Centre Mall, ☏ +91 03534503206 (Times Square Building), +91 353 257 6232 (City Centre), fabindia.vegacircle@gmail.com. Daily 11AM-9PM. Gifts and clothing store. (updated Jan 2018)
2 Shree Buddha Handicrafts, Sevoke Road, Panitanki, ☏ +91 97333 29274. A wholesaler and order supplier of Buddhist ritual handicrafts and other religious items. (updated Jan 2018)
3 Tanias Collection, Bidhan Market, ☏ +91 98320 34561. An eclectic mix of handcrafts, including religious statues. (updated Jan 2018)
4 Tashi Takgye, Metro Heights, Sevoke Road (near check post), ☏ +91 9434007076. A large store, specializing in Buddha statues, malas, and Buddhist ritual objects. (updated Aug 2026)


=== Tea ===
5 Chaichun, GF, Planet Mall, Sevoke Road (diagonally across from Cosmos), ☏ +91 93827 02318, ch6@chaichun.in. A modern shop selling traditional Indian teas, flavoured teas, Indian oolong, and tea-making equipment and accessories. (updated Aug 2026)
6 Chaichun Tea Experience Room, GF, Quantum Building, Paribahan Nagar, Matigara, ☏ +91 8016111507. Daily: 10AM-10PM. An elegant shop and tea room. Large selection of teas. Tasting available. (updated Sep 2026)
7 The Tea Cottage, Shivmandir, Military Road, ☏ +91 94345 54741. Excellent selection of Darjeeling and Assam teas at retail and wholesale prices. (updated Jan 2018)
8 Siliguri Tea Auction Committee, Mallaguri, Pradhan Nagar, info@siliguriteaauction.com. Tue-Sat 9AM–5PM. A place to make bulk purchases of Darjeeling and other locally grown teas. (updated Jan 2018)


=== Malls ===

9 City Centre (The Uttorayon Township), Matigara, NH-31. The largest mall in Siliguri, offering major brands, including a branch of Decathlon. International chain eateries. Cafes. Bars. Live music events. (updated Aug 2026)
10 City Mall, Service Road, Ward 13, Punjabi Para. Unassuming mall featuring local shops selling traditional clothing & jewelry, plus fast food. (updated Jan 2017)
11 Cosmos Mall, Sevoke Road, ☏ +91 353 254 5143, kamlesh.sahu@fmnl.in. Daily 10AM–10PM. Mall with a Big Bazaar store, plus fashion, cosmetics & home retailers, eateries & frequent events. (updated Jan 2017)
12 ML Acropolis Mall, Sevoke Road (Opp Anandaloke Hospital). A large mall featuring high-end commercial outlets, pub with live music; and movie complex. (updated Aug 2026)
13 Planet Mall, Sevoke Road (vertically opposite Cosmos Mall). A modern complex filled with pubs, restaurant, and cafes. A very happening place for the under 40s. (updated Jan 2022)
14 Vega Circle Mall, Nimbu Basti, vega@vegacircle.com. Daily 10:30AM–9PM. Chic and stylish. Home to an INOX movie theatre. Hotel. International stores, including Hamleys, H&M, and Marks and Spencers. Restaurants. Cafes. Bars. (updated Aug 2026)


=== Street markets ===
15 Bidhan Market, Ward 11, Hakim Para (near the Kanchenjunga Stadium). Daily noon–9PM. The oldest and largest street market in Siliguri, Bidhan Market meanders along streets and alleys and is particularly bustling and atmospheric at night. (updated Oct 2016)
16 Hong Kong Market, 6, Satyajit Roy Colony Road, Ward 41, Don Bosco Colony. Tue-Sun 9:30AM–9:30PM. Lively, long-standing market for bargain clothing, electronics & cosmetics, plus food vendors. However, beware of duplicate items. Even items made in Delhi stamped with "Made in China" are being sold here. The actual price of the item will be 1/2 or 1/3rd of the price the shopkeeper asks. (updated Oct 2016)
17 Seth Srilal Market, Ward 11, Hakim Para. Daily noon–9PM. Buzzing market in the heart of the city, where you might get the best deals. Also famous for its Momo Gali (Momo Street). (updated Oct 2016)


== Eat ==

Due to the large number of Nepalese and Tibetans living in Siliguri, the city offers an excellent selection of authentic Tibetan and Nepali delicacies. In addition, there are also several good quality restaurants specializing in Western and Chinese cuisine as well as a considerable number of US fast food outlets.


=== Budget ===
1 Khana Khajana, Hill Cart Road, Pradhan Nagar (Opp Tenzing Norgay Bus Station, next to Hotel Mountain View), ☏ +91 353 251 7516. Northern and Southern Indian Indian fast food. Outdoor seating at night.. Average food. Quick service. Convenient for Tenzing Norgay Bus Station and Siliguri Jn. (updated Aug 2026)
2 Momo Gali, Seth Srilal Market (near Margaret School, within easy walking distance of Siliguri Bus Stand). Daily 10AM-10PM. A street of restaurants and stalls selling fantastic momos. (updated Oct 2016)


=== Mid-range ===
3 Badshah Biryani Hut, Opposite Kanchenjunga Stadium, Khudiram Pally Road, Ward 11, Hakim Para, ☏ +91 81013 47809. Daily noon–10:30PM. Excellent Biriyani along with several other cuisines. 
4 Bedween Restaurant, Bidhan Market, Old Bus Stand, ☏ +91 98323 71558. Daily 10AM–10:30PM. Known for its delicious Biryani. 
5 Bhojohari Manna (Hotel Golden Moments), 143 Hill Cart Road, ☏ +91 94342 10011. Daily noon–10PM. Bengali cuisine. 
6 Cinderella Hotel, 3rd Mile, Sevoke Rd, ☏ +91 353 254 4130, +91 35325 47136. Amrapali - Vegetarian multi-cuisine restaurant, Recoil - Bar, Sizzler - discotheque for private parties, Patio - Roof-top restaurant-cum-bar. 
7 Havelli, Hill Cart Road, ☏ +91 353 253 5013. Daily 11AM–11PM. An excellent restaurant for fish and mutton items. Also offers high standard Chinese and continental dishes. Cool decor. 
8 Hi Spirits Cafe and Pub, 2nd floor City Centre, Uttorayon, ☏ +91 98320 59826. Daily noon–11PM. Low-key bar & restaurant in an unpretentious, no-frills ambience with Lebanese, Mexican, Chinese and Tibetan dishes cooked to a very high standard and live music 
9 Indian Pagoda, Top Plaza, Ground Floor, Sevoke Road. Daily 10am–11pm. Contemporary space serving a typical menu of popular Indianised Chinese dishes. (updated Jan 2022)
10 Kalpana Hotel Bengali Cuisines, Bidhan Market (Near Siliguri Town railway station), ☏ +91 76796 38292. Daily 10AM–9PM. Bengali cuisine 
11 Kalpatru Pice Restaurant, Panitanki More, Sevoke Road, Ashram Para, Hakim Para, ☏ +91 353 264 3479. Daily 10AM–10:30PM. Bengali cuisine 
12 Lama by Yeti, 3F Vega Circle Mall, Sevoke Road. Sun-Fri: Noon-11:45PM, Sat: Noon-1:45AM. Authentic Bhutanese, Nepalese, and Tibetan cuisine. Simple and elegant interior (updated Aug 2026)
13 Little Tokyo, 3F, Planet Mall, Sevoke Road, ☏ +91 96418 63365, little.tokyo.siliguri@gmail.com. Daily Noon–11PM. Authentic Vietnamese, Japanese, Thai, and Korean Food. Excellent sushi and mochi ice-cream. Stylish, East Asian themed interior. 
14 Marina's Motel, Bihar More, Bagdogra, ☏ +91 96097 43399, reservationmarinas@gmail.com. A serene motel in a colonial-style building with a furnished terrace and garden. Serves northern Indian and Chinese cuisine. Private dining available. (updated Jan 2022)
15 Monarch Restaurant, 10 Sevoke Road, ☏ +91 98320 62155. Daily 8AM–11:30PM. Famous for Indian, Tandoori and Chinese dishes. 
16 New Zaika Biryani House, Hill Cart Road, ☏ +91 94346 89708. Daily 9AM–11:15PM. Mughlai dishes 
17 Punjabi Kadhai, Sidhi Arcade, 2nd Mile, Sevoke Road, ☏ +91 98326 45678, info@punjabikadhai.in. Daily 11AM–11:11PM. Biryani, kebabs & other North Indian standards served in a casual, family-friendly rooftop setting. 
18 Sagar Family Restaurant, GF., Spacetown Appts, Check Post, 2nd Mile, Sevoke Road, ☏ +91 98320 77344, care@sagarfamilyslg.com. Daily: 2PM - 1O:45PM. Pure vegetarian. Specializes in North Indian cuisine. South Indian and Chinese meals available. Large, modern interior. Very clean. Welcoming and fast service. Excellent food. (updated May 2025)
19 Sartaj, 110/156, Hill Cart Road, ☏ +91 94325 16825. Daily 10AM–10:45PM. Good food, good ambience 
20 Steamy Moktu, 1F Planet Mall, Sevoke Road, ☏ +91 86950 86958, steamymoktusiliguri@gmail.com. Daily noon–10PM. Asian fusion restaurant, specializing in Thai and Chinese cuisine. (updated Apr 2018)
21 Tai Wah Restaurant, 2F. Sri Bhavan building, Hill Cart Road (Near Sevoke More. In dark alley opp Hotel Bidhan Plaza.), ☏ +91 353 243 6132. Daily 11AM–10PM. With a history dating from 1990, Taiwah is Siliguri’s oldest Chinese restaurant. Authentic Chinese cuisine and fusion dishes. Homey, low-key ambience. (updated May 2025)
22 The Basiil, 1st Floor, E Block, City Centre Mall (Above Domino's Pizza), ☏ +91 81670 86888, thebasiilslg@gmail.com. Daily: 10:30AM-11PM. Pure vegetarian: North Indian, Chinese, Continental, and Tandoor dishes. Cocktails and Mocktails. Tasteful and warm decor. Chair and floor seating. (updated Aug 2026)
23 The Palms (Sinclairs), Ward 46, Pradhan Nagar, ☏ +91 97334 62777, toll-free:  1800 120 267000, siliguri@sinclairshotels.com. 7:30AM to 11PM. Also: O3 lounge bar, 5-10:30PM. 
24 Taste of Sikkim, 3rd Mile, Sevoke Road, Salugara Bazar, Salugara. Daily 10AM–10PM. Simple and authentic Tibetan cuisine 
25 Viramma, Viramma Resort, Dagapur, ☏ +91 353 251 2222. A dining area in a resort. 


=== Splurge ===
26 G.O.A.T., 4F, Times Square, Sevoke Road, ☏ +91 91444 08801. Run by Indian football legend, Baichung Bhutia. Elevated dining and cocktails. Elegant interior. Roof top dining and bar. Live music. (updated Aug 2026)
27 Tea Pot, Mayfair Resort, New Chumta Tea Garden, Sevoke Road, Sukna, ☏ +91 3536660101. Daily: 12:30-15:30 and 19:00-22:30. A high standard multi-cuisine restaurant. Classic European interior. Excellent service. (updated Aug 2026)


== Drink ==


=== Coffee ===
As Siliguri is at the heart of a tea-growing area, it has traditionally been associated with tea. However, following the international trend, coffee culture has made inroads in the city and there are now numerous branches of cafe chains as well as a large number of independent coffee shops in and around Siliguri, and the quality of the coffee served is generally very good. Due to the large number of cafes in Siliguri, only those with a distinct character are listed here. 

1 Bake Walk, GF. Planet Mall, Sevoke Road.. 11AM-9PM. Warm and inviting interior. Excellent pastries and coffee. Pottery and unusual items, like organic body scrubs and bamboo toothbrushes, on sale. Serves light vegetarian meals, such as pasta, waffles, and toast-based dishes. 
2 Barista, Vega Circle Mall and City Centre, information@barista.co.in. 10AM-10PM daily. A cafe chain. The City Centre branch is a proper cafe, whereas the Vega Circle one is open plan (updated Feb 2021)
3 Berlin Kaffeehaus, City Centre Mall (near Pizza Hut), ☏ +91 98000 45601. An open and light cafe. Outdoor seating, Delicious pastries and cakes. Excellent coffee. (updated Aug 2026)
4 Brewberry Cafe, Nazrul Sarani, Ashram Para, Hakim Para (Ten minute walk from PaniTanki More). Large space. Restaurant-style design. Excellent fusion cuisine. Open 24 hours. (updated Aug 2026)
5 Café Coffee Day, Cosmos Mall, Sevoke Road, ☏ +91 353 320 1907, customercare@cafecoffeeday.com. A coffee chain, selling affordable coffee and pasties. Open plan seating (updated Jan 2022)
6 Cafe Karmaa Diaries, Sidhi Arcade Building, Sevoke Road, Dasrath Pally, Bhanu Nagar (near Anandaloke Nursing Home), ☏ +91 98002 62678. Mon 12:30PM-midnight, Tue-Sun noon-midnight. Touted as Siliguri's first mindfulness cafe. Buddhist quotes on walls, Excellent international cuisine. Coffee. Restaurant-style setting. Glass roof. Wish-fulfilling tree (updated Aug 2026)
7 Cafe The Twins, Methibari, Salbari, ☏ +91 97332 37209. Daily: 10:30AM-8PM. A woman-led book book-café. Cozy vibe. English, Nepali, Bengali books. Good coffee. Tasty and healthy meals. (updated Sep 2026)
8 Dakini Cafe, BSF Road, Salugara (heading towards Coronation Bridge on Sevoke Road, cafe is an alley on the right, just after Tashi Gomang Stupa), ☏ +91 98325 04696. Mon-Sat 11:30AM-9:30PM, Sun 11:30AM-8:30PM. A cool, open cafe with brick walls, plants, wooden floors, and various Tibetan Buddhist art and symbols. Great coffee. Excellent Italian cuisine. (updated Aug 2026)
9 Ovenly, Swamiji More, Nazrul Sarani, Ashrampara, ☏ +91 70014 45897. Noon to midnight. A small bakery-cafe specializing in custom-made cakes and pastries. (updated Nov 2018)
 Starbucks, Vega Circle Mall, City Centre Mall.. From Seattle to Siliguri the same interior design and coffee. 
10 The April, Debi Chaudhurani Road, Salugara (near Rose Valley apartment), ☏ +91 86538 86811. 11:00-21:00. A large cafe in a single story building. Outdoor and indoor seating. Modern and chic. Bright. Lots of plants. Excellent coffee. Good cafe-style menu. Small selection of books. (updated Aug 2026)
11 The Coffee Shop, 3F Vega Circle Mall, Salugara., ☏ +91 89727 72026. 10AM-10PM. An open plan cafe with large screens showing sport events. Espresso-based coffees. Pastries. Specialises in Italian food. (updated Aug 2018)


=== Tea ===
12 Netaji Cabin, Bidhan Market, ☏ +91 94342 47564. 6AM-9:15PM. A traditional tea store with great breakfast menu. (updated Jan 2022)


=== Alcohol ===

With a young, educated, and liberal population, Siliguri enjoys a vibrant and lively pub scene. Planet Mall is the city's main watering hole, and there are a number of pubs and cafes throughout the mall

13 O3 (Sinclairs lounge), Ward 46, Pradhan Nagar, ☏ +91 97334 62777, toll-free:  1800 120 267000, siliguri@sinclairshotels.com. 7:30AM to 10:30PM. Worth checking out for a nice evening drink and snacks. (updated Jan 2022)
14 Hashtag, 3F, Planet Mall, Sevoke Road, ☏ +91 98320 99995. M-F: 12PM-12AM, Sa: 12PM-2AM, Su: 12PM-1AM. Trendy, upscale bar. Warm lighting. Dance floor. Japanese, Continental, and Indian cuisine. Large selection of drinks. (updated Sep 2026)

== Stay safe ==
As elsewhere in India, travellers may encounter scams and touts. Be wary of anyone offering unsolicited directions or travel advice, and avoid openly indicating that this is your first visit to the city.
If you are arriving after midnight, it is advisable to book accommodation in advance and arrange a pick-up from the bus terminal or railway station.
Overall, Siliguri is an extremely safe city with a very low crime rate, and violent crime against international travellers is unheard of.

== Connect ==
Cell phone coverage in the city is excellent. There are three major service providers offering a wide variety of plans. Among them are Airtel, VI (formerly Vodafone) and Jio. Airtel is the preferable one as it provides high quality calls and great internet speed all across the city.
To call Siliguri from abroad you will need to dial the international prefix for your country, followed by India's country code +91. If you want to dial a landline no. from a mobile, then you have to add the area code of Siliguri, 0353 before the number.
Internet services are unreliable in some parts of the city. Most stores have broadband connections. Both the railway stations have free high-speed Wi-fi services but you need an Indian mobile number to register and receive the one-time password.

== Go next ==
Bodh Gaya - By bus, daily service offered Jay Jagdambey Bus Company. 3PM from Tenzing Norgay Bus Station (in front of Gupta Tour and Travels). A/C sleeper. Approx ₹700. 17 hours.  Sri Krishna Rath Bus Company. 8:30PM.  Tenzin Norgay Bus Station. A/C sleeper Between approx  ₹1,600-₹2,000 (depending on seat design) 14 hours.
Darjeeling — one of the oldest hill stations in India with interesting sites as well as trekking opportunities. Tu, Th Sa 8:30AM, Toy train (https://www.darjeeling-tourism.com/darj_00009e.htm) departs NJP Station stopping at Siliguri Jn. Between ₹1,420-1,700 for the just over 7 hours journey.
Gangtok — this hill station is a popular site as a jumping-off point for treks, the home of the Banjhakri Falls, views of surrounding mountains and friendly atmosphere. ₹400 for shared taxi from Tenzing Norgay bus station (a little more from NJP Station).
Gompa Dara — a small village that is the site of Gompa Rock and meditation caves and the Ogyen Mindrol Samtenling (Buddhist monastery)
Jalpaiguri — a city with many historical links to the past
Jaldapara National Park —  this national park is a 180-min drive from Siliguri. It's famous for its wildlife, in particular the Indian rhinoceros, bison, elephants, and peacocks.
Kalimpong — a hill station with many gardens and religious sites. Buses depart Tenzing Norgay bus station and NJP train station every 20 minutes until 4PM - ₹110-130 for the two and a half hour journey (little more from NJP). Shared and private jeeps also ply the route from the same locations - approx ₹300 and ₹2,800/₹3,000 respectively.
Kathmandu. The Indian border town of Panitanki is around one hour from Siliguri. From there, it is 1.7 km to the Nepalese border town of Kakarbhitta (rickshaws available).   The Nepal-Indian border at Siliguri, which was only open to Bhutanese, Indian, and Nepalese passport holders since the pandemic, is now open to all passport holders with valid visas (updated May 2025)  Green Line Bus Service operates a daily overnight A/C Volvo bus service from Siliguri (Tenzing Norgay Bus Station) to Kathmandu (Swayambhu Bus Stand). Departs at 3PM, arriving at 8:30AM. ₹2,000. Tickets from North Point Tours and Treks in Tenzin Norgay Bus Station. (8972422958 / 8116781792). As the road conditions in Nepal are precarious, it is advisable to contact the agent prior to traveling to Siliguri to ensure the bus is running, especially during the monsoon.
Lava — a hamlet surrounded by  beautiful natural forests. Home to the Lava Monastery and a spot to view Kanchenjunga peak at sunrise.
Loleygaon (Lolegaon) — a village noted for its Canopy Walk, Jhandi Dhara Sunrise Point, and Lolegaon View Point.
Mangpoo — a small village (hill station) with beautiful views was once known for its medicinal plant cultivation. It was the site where poet laureate Rabindranath Tagore wrote his famous poem Janmadine.
Mirik — a hill station with scenic views and tea gardens. The town is home to Sumendu Lake, several religious sites, and the international Bokar Buddhist Meditation Centre.
Phuentsholing — Khorlo/Dophu Transport +91 9832071965. Daily: 7AM (Coaster bus), noon (Coaster bus), 2PM (Eicher bus) from opposite Golden Plaza on Burdwan Road (behind Air View More). Tickets are sold at a counter near the bus parking area, and it costs ₹350 for the four-hour journey. +91 9832071965 See 'Go next' on Siliguri page for more information.  There are more frequent Indian buses to the border town of Jaigaon from Tenzing Norgay Bus Station on Hill Cart Road. In addition, trains depart Silguri Junction at 7:45AM and 1PM (local - around 4 hours) and 8:15AM and 12:30PM (express - around 3 hours) to Hasimara, from where an auto (shared - around ₹30-50, reserved - around ₹300) can be taken to Jaigoan - 20 minutes. Foreign nationals need to complete Indian immigration formalities before entering Bhutan, and so need to alight the bus or auto at the immigration office in Jaigaon. (June 2026)
